approach: Teach hay as one survival word that asks and answers whether something is there, with the answers a learner will actually hear (no hay, ya no hay), then practice in a shop and a restaurant.
coverage: Hay means there is or there are, and sounds like the English word "eye"
The same word works for one or many: hay un baño, hay dos baños
¿Hay baño? ¿Hay agua? ask whether something exists or is available
No hay means there is not, there are none
Ya no hay means there is no more, it has run out
Answers: Sí, hay. / No, no hay.

blocks.purpose: Defines hay and its pronunciation in one card.

data.anchor: Hay (said like the English word "eye") means "there is" or "there are", and with a question mark it asks whether something is there.
prerequisites: The h is silent, so hay sounds like "eye".
One word for one or many: Hay un baño. Hay dos baños.
Answer: Sí, hay. (Yes, there is.) / No, no hay. (No, there isn't.)

data.prompt: You want to know if a café has wifi. What do you ask?

feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Read the feedback and try again.

byOption.a: Yes: hay asks whether something is there or available.
byOption.b: Tengo means I have. You would be asking whether you have wifi.
byOption.c: Voy means I am going. It does not fit here.
byOption.d: This is a statement: there is no more wifi. It does not ask anything.

data.question: How do you say hay?

trapReasons.1: Hay is also an English word (dried grass), so the eye reads it in English.

data.whyIntuitionFailed: The word is spelled like an English word, so the English sound comes first.
data.correctReasoning: The h is silent and a + y blend into one sound: "eye".
data.recoveryTip: Hay sounds like the English word "eye".

blocks.purpose: Closes with hay as a single word for asking and answering about what is there.

data.takeaway: ¿Hay ...? asks if something is there; sí, hay says yes; no hay says none; ya no hay says it has run out.

checks.prompt: A waiter says "Ya no hay pollo." What does he mean?
checks.rationale: Ya no hay means there is no more: the chicken has run out. Pollo is chicken.

checks.rationale: Hay never changes: the same word means there is and there are.
